docs.title: GRC Auto-Arrange
docs.text: Intelligent, automated block placement and flowgraph beautifier for GNU Radio Companion (GRC) powered by the Eclipse Layout Kernel (ELK).

docs.title: ⚡ Interactive Live Demo
docs.text:
Watch messy, tangled flowgraphs automatically arrange into an optimal layered DAG with zero cable crossings:

⚠️ Messy Flowgraph (Unarranged) GNU Radio Companion Canvas Simulation ⚡ Auto-Arrange (Ctrl+Shift+A)

docs.title: 📸 GNU Radio Companion Before & After
docs.text:
See the actual GNU Radio Companion 3.10 interface before and after running Auto-Arrange Flowgraph:

✨ After Auto-Arrange (ELK Layered)⚠️ Before Auto-Arrange (Messy)🔍 Canvas Close-Up Comparison

After: Variables cleanly stacked in the top header row; signal processing flow structured left-to-right with straight orthogonal connections and 8px grid alignment.

Before: Blocks scattered randomly across the canvas with backwards routing, intersecting wires, and misaligned variables.

Before Auto-Arrange After Auto-Arrange Scattered blocks, tangled diagonal wires Clean layered DAG, variables in header banner

docs.title: 🚀 Key Highlights
docs.text:
• Direct GRC Integration

    Seamlessly adds Auto Arrange Flowgraph into GRC's Edit/Tools menu and toolbar. Press Ctrl + Shift + A to tidy up your canvas in real time.

  • Full Undo / Redo Support

    Integrated directly into GRC's native state history. Hit Ctrl + Z to roll back or Ctrl + Y to redo anytime.

  • Smart Block Categorization

    Automatically isolates configuration variables (samp_rate, cutoff, etc.) into a tidy top banner while structuring signal processing blocks into a left-to-right DAG.

  • 8px Grid Snapping

    All block coordinates strictly adhere to GNU Radio Companion's standard 8-pixel alignment grid for pixel-perfect wiring.

  • :material-terminal:{ .lg .middle } Headless CLI & Pre-Commit Hook

    Format .grc flowgraph files headlessly with grc-autoarrange -i flowgraph.grc or automate repository linting in CI/CD pipelines.

  • Zero NPM Dependencies

    Includes a bundled standalone Eclipse Layout Kernel (ELK) engine that runs effortlessly on any system with Node.js installed.

docs.title: 📦 Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Install2. Launch GRC with Auto-Arrange3. Or Format Headlessly 
pip install --user .

grc-autoarrange --gui my_flowgraph.grc

# Format in-place
grc-autoarrange -i my_flowgraph.grc

# Output to new file
grc-autoarrange input.grc -o output.grc

docs.title: Python API Reference
docs.text: grc_autoarrange provides a Python API for programmatic flowgraph analysis, layout configuration, and formatting.

docs.title: AutoArrangeSettings
docs.text:
Handles persistent user preferences and layout defaults.

from grc_autoarrange import AutoArrangeSettings

settings = AutoArrangeSettings(node_spacing=60, layer_spacing=80, direction="RIGHT")
settings.block_spacing = 72  # Convenience property setter
settings.save()  # Saves to ~/.config/gnuradio/grc_autoarrange.json

docs.title: Properties & Methods
docs.text:
• block_spacing: Get/set general block spacing (automatically updates node_spacing and scales layer_spacing).
  • save(file_path=None): Save settings to disk.
  • load(file_path=None): Load settings from disk with fallback to defaults.

docs.title: LayoutPlanner
docs.text:
from grc_autoarrange import LayoutPlanner, LayoutConfig

config = LayoutConfig(block_spacing=64)
planner = LayoutPlanner(config=config)

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: • arrange_flowgraph_data(data, selected_block_names=None, block_sizes=None): Computes new (x, y) coordinates for all blocks in the flowgraph.

docs.title: ElkEngine
docs.text:
Low-level wrapper executing the vendored ELK layout engine.

from grc_autoarrange import ElkEngine, ElkNode, ElkEdge, ElkPort

engine = ElkEngine()
nodes = [ElkNode(id="src", width=160, height=80), ElkNode(id="sink", width=160, height=80)]
edges = [ElkEdge(id="e1", source="src", target="sink")]
result = engine.layout(nodes, edges)

docs.title: Architecture & Layout Engine
docs.text: grc-autoarrange bridges GNU Radio Companion (GRC) with the Eclipse Layout Kernel (ELK), bringing state-of-the-art graph layout algorithms to software-defined radio flowgraphs.

docs.title: High-Level Pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Input Flowgraph] --> B[Block Categorizer]

    subgraph Categorization
        B --> C1[Header / Config Blocks]
        B --> C2[Signal Processing Graph]
        B --> C3[Floating Blocks]
    end

    subgraph Layout Engines
        C1 --> D1[Grid Placement Engine]
        C2 --> D2[ELK Layered Sugiyama Algorithm]
        C3 --> D3[Secondary Stacking Engine]
    end

    D1 --> E[Coordinate Aggregation & 8px Grid Snapping]
    D2 --> E
    D3 --> E

    E --> F1[Live GRC Canvas Redraw & Undo Stack]
    E --> F2[Serialized .grc YAML Output]

docs.title: 1. Block Classification
docs.text:
GNU Radio flowgraphs contain two fundamentally different kinds of blocks:

  1. Header / Configuration Blocks:
  2. options, variable, variable_qtgui_*, import, parameter, snippet.
  3. These blocks do not participate in sample streaming connections. Placing them inside the signal flow causes clutter.

  4. Solution: grc-autoarrange isolates them into a neat, wrapping header banner at the top of the canvas, starting with options at (16, 16).

  5. Signal Processing Blocks:

  6. Blocks with input (sink) or output (source) ports forming the processing pipeline (DAG).

  7. Routed to the ELK Layered Layout engine.

  8. Floating / Disconnected Blocks:

  9. Signal blocks without active connections are neatly stacked below the main diagram.

docs.title: 2. ELK Layered Layout & Port Constraints
docs.text:
The core signal DAG is laid out using ELK's Layered Algorithm (based on the Sugiyama framework):

  • Layer Assignment: Nodes are assigned to discrete horizontal layers according to signal flow.
  • Crossing Minimization (LAYER_SWEEP): Heuristic layer sweeping swaps node positions to minimize cable intersections.
  • Port Constraints (FIXED_POS):
  • Sink ports (inputs) are positioned on the WEST (left) edge.
  • Source ports (outputs) are positioned on the EAST (right) edge.
  • Message ports are appropriately oriented.
  • Coordinate Assignment (BRANDES_KOEPF): Calculates straight, aesthetic edge segments while respecting node heights and port positions.
  • Feedback Loops: Directed cycles (e.g. Costas loops, PLLs, feedback taps) are detected and routed with inverted feedback edges without breaking the layout.

docs.title: 3. Grid Snapping
docs.text:
GNU Radio Companion operates on an 8-pixel raster. grc-autoarrange applies snap_to_grid() to every calculated coordinate:

$$\text{coord}{\text{snapped}} = 8 \times \text{round}\left(\frac{\text{coord}\right)$$}}}{8

This ensures that port connections align with orthogonal wires and GRC's snap-to-grid UI behaves consistently.

docs.title: CLI & Batch Formatter Guide
docs.text: grc-autoarrange includes a standalone command-line interface for formatting .grc flowgraphs without launching the GUI.

docs.title: Command Syntax
docs.text: grc-autoarrange [OPTIONS] flowgraph.grc [flowgraph2.grc ...]

docs.title: Options Reference
docs.text: Flag Description Default -i, --in-place Overwrite input flowgraph files directly on disk. False -o, --output Write output to a specified .grc file path. stdout -s, --spacing, --block-spacing Set general block spacing (scales node & layer spacing). None (from config) --node-spacing Spacing between nodes in the same layer (pixels). 48 --layer-spacing Spacing between consecutive layers (pixels). 64 -d, --direction Flow direction: RIGHT, DOWN, LEFT, UP. RIGHT --header-columns Max number of columns in the header variable grid. None (auto-wrap) --save-defaults Save specified spacing and direction as persistent user defaults. False --gui Launch GNU Radio Companion with the Auto-Arrange addon. False --dry-run Calculate layout without modifying files. False -v, --verbose Print detailed step-by-step layout logging. False

docs.text: Compact Spacing (--spacing 24) Spacious Layout (--spacing 96)

docs.title: 1. In-Place Formatting with Custom Spacing
docs.text:
Format a flowgraph file directly with custom block spacing: 

grc-autoarrange -i my_receiver.grc --spacing 60

docs.title: 2. Output to a New File
docs.text:
Format and save as a separate copy: 

grc-autoarrange messy.grc -o clean.grc

docs.title: 3. Save Default Spacing Preferences
docs.text:
Save your preferred block spacing persistently so all future GUI and CLI formatting runs use it automatically: 

grc-autoarrange --spacing 72 --save-defaults

docs.title: 4. Custom Spacing & Vertical Flow
docs.text:
Arrange with top-to-bottom layout and larger spacing: 

grc-autoarrange input.grc -o output.grc --direction DOWN --node-spacing 80 --layer-spacing 100

docs.title: 5. Dry Run & Verification
docs.text:
Verify layout calculations without writing changes: 

grc-autoarrange --dry-run my_flowgraph.grc

docs.title: Pre-Commit Hook Integration
docs.text:
You can easily add grc-autoarrange to your .pre-commit-config.yaml to ensure all GNU Radio flowgraphs in your repository remain formatted:

repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: grc-autoarrange
        name: Auto-arrange GNU Radio Flowgraphs
        entry: grc-autoarrange -i --spacing 48
        language: python
        types: [yaml]
        files: \.grc$

docs.title: GNU Radio Companion GUI Addon
docs.text: grc-autoarrange includes native GUI hooks for GNU Radio Companion (GRC). It adds menu options, a settings dialog, a toolbar button, keyboard shortcuts, and full undo/redo integration directly within GRC's GTK3 canvas.

docs.title: Visual Comparison
docs.text:
• Before Auto-Arrange

docs.title: Launching GRC with Auto-Arrange
docs.text:
To launch GNU Radio Companion with the Auto-Arrange addon enabled:

grc-autoarrange --gui [flowgraph.grc]

docs.title: Configurable Spacing & Settings Dialog
docs.text: You can customize block spacing, layer spacing, and layout direction dynamically from within GRC via Edit → Auto Arrange Settings...:

docs.title: Settings Options
docs.text:
• Block Spacing (Vertical / Same Layer): Control vertical spacing between blocks in the same layer (8px to 300px).
  • Layer Spacing (Horizontal / Between Layers): Control spacing between consecutive processing stages (8px to 400px).
  • Flow Direction: Choose RIGHT (standard left-to-right), DOWN (top-to-bottom), LEFT, or UP.
  • Header Columns: Set fixed column count for top variable header or 0 for auto-wrap.
  • Save as Default: Persists your preferences to ~/.config/gnuradio/grc_autoarrange.json so every future session uses them.

docs.title: Spacing Comparison Examples
docs.text:
Adjusting block spacing allows you to optimize for tight, compact canvas views or spacious, easily readable diagrams:

🔹 Compact Spacing (Spacing: 24px)🔸 Spacious Layout (Spacing: 96px)🔍 Side-by-Side Canvas View

Compact Spacing: Ideal for complex, multi-stage flowgraphs to fit maximum components on screen without overlapping.

Spacious Layout: Provides ample room between processing blocks and clear separation of parallel branches.

Compact Spacing (--spacing 24) Spacious Layout (--spacing 96) Tight, space-efficient block arrangement Wide separation for complex feedback paths

docs.title: Selection-Only Layout
docs.text:
If your flowgraph is large and you only want to organize a localized portion (e.g. a demodulator subsystem):

  1. Select the blocks you want to organize by dragging a selection rectangle or holding Ctrl and clicking.
  2. Press Ctrl + Shift + A.
  3. Only the selected blocks will be arranged relative to each other; all unselected blocks remain untouched!

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • GNU Radio 3.8+ / 3.10+ (with GNU Radio Companion installed)
  • Node.js runtime (node binary available on your PATH).

Node.js Requirement

grc-autoarrange uses the Eclipse Layout Kernel (ELK). The full ELK engine bundle (elk.bundled.js) is self-contained inside the Python package, meaning you do not need to run npm install. You only need the standard node interpreter installed on your system.

docs.title: User Installation (Recommended)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/tfcollins/grc-autoarrange.git
cd grc-autoarrange
pip install --user .

docs.title: Editable Development Installation
docs.text:
If you are developing or customizing the layout rules:

pip install --user -e .

docs.title: Verifying the Installation
docs.text:
Verify that the CLI executable is available in your shell:

grc-autoarrange --help

You should see the help menu with options like --gui, -i/--in-place, -d/--direction, and spacing controls.
